review: Read complete chat store, memory registry and all five related tests; shared chat/registry type definitions also inspected as omitted dependencies.

Chat sessions, current selection and cached task-binding projections use profile-specific storage. Unknown account identity, signed-out guest and named accounts have separate keys. Account events swap the in-memory store and persistence key together; legacy shared storage remains unclaimed.
Registry metadata follows the same profile key transition before chat artifacts are registered. This indexes storage and is not authorization for a server read, pairing, model run or game action.

appendMessageOnce suppresses duplicate IDs and preserves existing content on conflicts; only matching terminal-projection identity and recognized truncated-prefix shape can restore a saved long message. The UI helper itself does not cryptographically validate terminal evidence; its upstream producer remains responsible.

Chat persistence bounds saved sessions/message lengths and retries with smaller representations under quota pressure. Cached bindings remain projections, not current authority. Synthetic alpha/beta fixtures contain no live account messages or credentials.
No canonical source edits. Proposed exports are the existing source used by R379; normalization is line endings only.
limits: Private source proposal only; no commit, push or new build.
Focused local-store tests cannot prove cross-device sync, complete transcript durability, server authorization or live friend delivery.
Existing concurrent-session test unchanged in public preview.
Account policy is an earlier reviewed export dependency. Shared schemas and external dependencies remain separate source inputs.
